summary: Ten concrete recommendations from a complete 30-story HN front-page comment crawl.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: The Cuckoo's Egg
items.source_story_title: Stalking the Wily Hacker: 40 years later – Cliff Stoll [video]
items.summary: Cliff Stoll's true account of tracking a hacker through early computer networks.
items.why_included: A reader singled it out as a rare genuine page-turner and praised the writing.
items.evidence: A reader called the book an exceptional page-turner and fantastically well written.

evidence_sources.author: nevster
evidence_sources.excerpt: The Cuckoo's Egg is the exception. Such a fantastically well-written book!

items.name: Muppet Treasure Island BTS video
items.summary: Behind-the-scenes footage featuring Tim Curry during Muppet Treasure Island.
items.why_included: A commenter was glad they watched it and paired it with strong praise for the film.
items.evidence: The commenter called Muppet Treasure Island Curry's best work and welcomed the behind-the-scenes video.

evidence_sources.author: billbrown
evidence_sources.excerpt: For me, his best work was Muppet Treasure Island. I'm glad I watched this BTS video with him

items.name: Fira Sans
items.summary: A free, characterful sans-serif family originally designed with Mozilla.
items.why_included: A commenter called it their go-to sans serif and praised its distinctive character.
items.evidence: A regular user described Fira Sans as their go-to and praised its character.

evidence_sources.author: ashton314
evidence_sources.excerpt: I also love the pure character of Fira Sans and it’s my go-to sans serif.

items.name: Pigeons
items.source_story_title: Tailcat – Like netcat, but over Tailscale’s data plane
items.summary: SSH access through NAT or firewalls without port forwarding or VPN setup.
items.why_included: A homelab user relies on it extensively for access and service tunnels.
items.evidence: A commenter reported extensive homelab use for SSH access plus SMB and Postgres tunneling.

evidence_sources.author: Arqu
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use it in my homelab extensivelly for access, tunneling smb, postgres and some other minor bits.

items.name: ha-bambulab
items.summary: A Home Assistant integration for monitoring and automating Bambu Lab printers.
items.why_included: A frequent user called it excellent for printer monitoring and event automation.
items.evidence: A commenter uses the integration constantly and praised its monitoring and automation support.

evidence_sources.author: hamdingers
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's excellent for monitoring and setting up automations around printer events, I use it all the time too.

items.name: Yesterdays
items.source_story_title: Oldinsurancemaps.net is now a Charter Project
items.summary: An interactive map connecting historical photos with Sanborn maps and locations.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it to fans of historical insurance maps.
items.evidence: The recommendation highlighted its use of Sanborn maps to place historical photos accurately.

evidence_sources.author: lapetitejort
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you like OldInsuranceMaps, check out another OSM charter project, Yesterdays!

items.name: Bitsavers IBM 7950/HARVEST archive
items.source_story_title: Harvest (IBM 7950): Supercomputer for cryptanalysis at the NSA in the Cold War
items.summary: Primary manuals and documents for IBM's Cold War HARVEST cryptanalysis system.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly praised Bitsavers while pointing readers to the primary sources.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended the IBM 7950 collection as excellent primary-source material.

evidence_sources.author: nxobject
evidence_sources.excerpt: Primary sources for the IBM 7950/HARVEST on Bitsavers, excellent as always

items.name: hraness kb
items.source_story_title: Agentic Context Management: Memory and Cost as Architecture Problems
items.summary: A Markdown agent knowledge base with backlinks, semantic search, and Git context.
items.why_included: Its author says this simple repository pattern is sufficient for their coding and non-coding agents.
items.evidence: The maintainer reported that a Markdown knowledge base is all they need to improve agent memory.

evidence_sources.author: benzguo
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've found that a simple markdown knowledgebase (with some useful extensions like semantic search & git context) is all I need to improve the memory of my agents.

items.name: Enterprise Document Intelligence
items.source_story_title: RAG Is Simpler Than You Think
items.summary: A practical series building enterprise RAG from a minimal pipeline to production.
items.why_included: A practitioner struggling with RAG recommended the series and found it useful.
items.evidence: A reader explicitly recommended Angela Shi's enterprise-document series after finding it useful.

evidence_sources.author: Otterly99
evidence_sources.excerpt: I would recommend this author that has whole series on entreprise documents (start with the one from May 22nd)

items.name: SQLar
items.summary: A ZIP-like archive format and tool built on an ordinary SQLite database.
items.why_included: A commenter highlighted SQLite archives while calling the underlying application-file idea compelling.
items.evidence: The commenter presented SQLar as a ZIP-like SQLite archive and endorsed the broader idea as compelling.

evidence_sources.author: ramses0
evidence_sources.excerpt: SQLar - https://sqlite.org/sqlar/doc/trunk/README.md ...basically `s/zip/sqlar/g` and you're not that far off.
